govdocs-archive_org-nsia-BreedenArthur_B: This FBI report on Lee Harvey Oswald — Internal Security, Cuba — is a Bureau file on the accused assassin. The declassified report is a primary source. Oswald’s Cuba ties fascinated investigators. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CubanBoatSeizur: Marilyn Berger’s Washington Post piece — U.S. Renews Denials of Any Role in Cuban Boat Seizures — covers the diplomatic row. Denials were routine. The Cold War ran hot at sea. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MillerArthur_Mi: This letter to Arthur Miller — August 29, 1968, creator unknown — is a personal note. Miller was the great American playwright. The note may hold a clue. The file belongs to the literary archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
in-the-court-of-king-arthur: Samuel Edward Lowe retells the great Arthurian legends for young readers — Arthur and his knights, Merlin's magic, the quest for the Holy Grail. The timeless tales of Camelot appear in clear, stirring prose meant to thrill boys and girls meeting them for the first time. A fine doorway into the noblest stories of English legend.
the-louisa-alcott-reader-a-supplementary: The Louisa Alcott Reader gathers the beloved author's best for fourth-year schoolchildren — scenes from Little Women and other favorites, adapted for young readers. Generations first met Jo, Meg, and Laurie through these schoolroom pages. A classroom classic of American childhood.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-assur: A 1913 entry on Assur — Ashur, the Assyrian capital. Gabriel Oussani tells its mighty story. Its ziggurat crowned the Tigris. The empire's gods dwelt in its temples. The first city of the Assyrians. Its ruins crown the Tigris bluff. Its priests served the great gods.
